cc: "margaret.thomas@lumieresante.fr" <margaret.thomas@lumieresante.fr>
Subject: RE: Saint-Hilaire Clinic


Dear Aimé / Margaret,

Thank you for visiting Montclair to present the clinical initiatives. It was a
pleasure meeting your team and we look forward to collaborating with Lumière
Santé. Please also extend our gratitude for the dinner.

We wanted to update you on our research and gather feedback before our
upcoming visit to Saint-Hilaire Clinic on 17 January. Our study will focus on
the third approach you outlined. We aim to address part of the Health Services
division’s operations. We are considering two paths: (i) analyzing patient
intake procedures and recommending improvements for outpatient care, or (ii)
reviewing the medical supply chain and advising on potential investment areas.

However, we need additional details on the Outpatient Care Services before
finalizing the scope. We welcome any suggestions, especially if you envision a
broader or different focus; please let us know.

We have yet to review the initial documents sent last week, but here are some
questions specifically about the Health Services unit:

Could we access the overall business plan or a more detailed summary than the
annual report? What is the pricing strategy and general framework? Who are the
patients and how are they engaged? What alternatives do patients have if not
using Lumière Santé? What are the plans and capabilities for international
expansion? Is there any key regulatory information available?

If this is not already included in the materials you provided, could you
recommend other sources for this information?

Once we review the documents, we may want to arrange a call with you or a
colleague directly involved in Health Services. I will reach out in the new
year to discuss further. Meanwhile, feel free to contact me at +33 4 59 27 70
77 if you need anything.

Regards,
Outpatient Care Services Rapid Response Team
Ram
Dennis
Jason
Omar
Steve
Clay

This basically follows how we managed it last year, except now they’re separating Origination and Portfolio teams. The biggest challenge remains how to integrate Atlas and avoid the manual Atlas-spreadsheet-Atlas cycle we had last year. We’re collaborating with Hannah Ferguson and the Atlas team on this.

Subject: Ironclad vs. TerraHaul, per Summit Freight
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Summit Freight's Ironclad first appeared a few years back as a premium upgrade
to the well-known TerraHaul bulk hauler. The issue was, TerraHaul’s model
could be just as well-equipped as the Ironclad and, in some trims, carried an
even higher price tag. For 2024, Summit Freight has worked to further set
their Ironclad apart from the popular TerraHaul. The end product is a robust
bulk logistics truck with enhanced handling and a wealth of advanced features.

This near-premium hauler is offered with either a 6.0-litre inline-six engine
producing 320 kilowatts or a 7.2-litre V8 delivering 385 kW. Both engines are
paired with a six-speed automatic transmission. The new V8 option provides
abundant and smooth power, though its fuel economy figures are modest. The
Ironclad has undergone a complete redesign both inside and out, and the
results are impressive. Easily distinguishable from the TerraHaul from the
front grille forward, it incorporates a distinctive "Steel Edge" design theme
featuring a matte-finish grille and aggressive LED headlamps. Inside,
satin-brushed aluminum trim accents create a modern, tech-forward feel that
distances the Ironclad from its TerraHaul origins.

The upgrades to the Ironclad extend far beyond aesthetics. A brand-new
independent rear suspension with a unique oval-cut frame design debuts this
year. This arrangement lowers the rear cargo floor by 180mm, allowing for a
larger payload area while increasing ground clearance to 235mm. At the same
time, ride comfort and handling have been greatly enhanced. The Ironclad now
offers noticeably improved stability on uneven terrain and exhibits flatter
cornering characteristics. A 65mm wider track further improves handling and
boosts the cabin space. Noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) levels have also
been reduced substantially in the 2024 Ironclad. Air infiltration into the cab
has been cut by 50%, and a refined transmission contributes to a quieter
driving experience, although some vibration from the available all-wheel-drive
system is still felt through the floor.

New convenience features on the Ironclad include a standard six-way
power-adjustable driver’s seat, with options for adjustable pedals, heated
front seats, and heated side mirrors. Safety enhancements include optional
side curtain airbags, a reinforced body frame, and a lower front bumper
designed to improve compatibility with other vehicles in collisions. Later
this year, rollover sensors and a new TractionPro traction and stability
control system will also be introduced.

The Ironclad’s strengths lie in its comprehensive feature set, powerful engine
options, and upgraded rear suspension. There are numerous haul trucks on the
market, but if you want a TerraHaul alternative that’s a step above the norm,
the Ironclad could be exactly what you’re looking for.

I can’t believe another year has gone by, but it has. Sunday, October 27th is the Juvenile Diabetes Convoy for Hope! Once again, I’m gathering drivers for my team or just asking for your support. I know you’re tired of constant fundraising asks, but I have to try—most of you know why! As someone managing insulin-dependent diabetes, it’s my duty to back every effort toward a cure affecting so many families. Many of you witness my daily routine of insulin shots and multiple glucose checks after meals. It’s been only 4 years since my diagnosis, but donations are making progress. In 2 years, they expect inhalable insulin to replace painful injections.

I realize you’ve been approached by many causes this year, but I hope you’ll keep Logistics for Hope among those you support as I do. Please join my convoy or one of the many BrasiLog teams to help find a cure for Diabetes! Every walker or sponsor donating R$25.00 or more will get a BrasiLog Logistics for Hope shirt! If R$25.00 is tight, you can buy a “Hope Badge” for just R$5.00, which will be displayed at the São Paulo Hub on October 25th. As always, BrasiLog matches contributions! Thanks for your support and hope to see you on the 27th!

-----Original Message-----
From: Bailey, Ann
Sent: Thursday, 7 November 2024 19:25
To: Cole, Elliot; Russell, Kirsty
Subject: Company Secretary Replacement

As you both probably know, I will officially retire on 31 December 2024; so
the meeting on 11 November will be my last and a good chance to appoint my
successor. Thanks for letting me stay on as your company secretary after
stepping down from that role at Halcyon Mutual Bank. I don’t think I could
have stopped “cold turkey,” and I loved Halcyon because of my fondness for
the board members and most of the senior team. (I’ll withhold comments on a
few former senior staff who are no longer here.) It’s been a real pleasure
since Hugh got involved, and the improved morale and financial results speak
volumes about the positive impact. I have also long admired Evergreen
Financial and enjoyed working with Oliver Leonard. It’s my sincere hope and
recommendation that Oliver be chosen to succeed me. He has repeatedly shown
he can handle the role — in fact, he’s been doing much of it for a long
time, except for the actual minute-taking, which he’s relieved me of more
than once. He’s a man of integrity, loyalty, and dedication, and I know the
board likes him. I hope you agree. I’ll miss you all, and Valerie, I’d love
to have lunch with you and Oliver anytime. I’m also happy to offer any
advice or support I can. Thanks again. Much love, Kathryn Archer

Subject: Catherine Storey for Corporate Advisory Client Reviews
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

I spoke with each of you a couple of weeks ago, but this matter was sidelined
due to more urgent issues. Still, everyone agreed that establishing a firm
deadline would be reasonable for finalising client reviews in Corporate,
Litigation, and Compliance.

The most practical approach is to set a daily cutoff at 4pm (to get a sense
of volume, I checked yesterday’s activity to see how many reviews were
completed after 4pm London Gilbert. There were three Corporate files and two
Litigation matters). After 4pm, the system would automatically carry forward
any pending client reviews to the next business day. However, for those cases
that don’t automatically roll over after 4pm, the respective teams must
remember these count as the following day’s workload.

I’m uncertain how the Compliance reporting procedures might need adjusting,
since the official daily records won’t reflect these late submissions. Could
Compliance generate supplementary reports to ensure the teams have accurate
statuses each morning?

Please send any feedback you have, and in any case, can you all confirm that
a 4pm cutoff is workable for your teams?

Danielle
x36557

Eric – do you foresee any issues with the Compliance reporting?
Mary – we touched on this briefly a few weeks ago… any further thoughts?

Klaus-Günter,
If we consider it from a Hamburg grid index perspective, how would this appear? I believe he wants to float a price linked to the grid index but needs some sense of the typical basis to Hamburg we would apply. It’s not a firm offer since he’s unlikely to proceed with a transaction, so it’s more a market indicator. A bit unusual, but the more competitive our price is relative to Hamburg, the better our chances of securing the contract. We should present him with a solid offer, subject to credit approval and other conditions. When it comes to finalising the deal, he probably won’t commit given the units lack historical output data, so the market price could be quite different then.

Arno

Subject: Kestrel/Strato Flag Football Invitation

Kestrel Aerospace and Strato Systems are proud to sponsor the 2nd Annual
Falcon-Eagle Flag Football Challenge on Saturday, November 16. The event
aims to raise funds for both organisations and celebrate the long-standing
rivalry in collegiate football. This marks the 107th meeting between Kestrel
Falcons and Strato Eagles, with the Big 12 South Title potentially at stake!

Kestrel and Strato Systems are sponsoring the event, but we need your
support as players and fundraisers. Proceeds will benefit the general
scholarship funds of the two schools.

The details:
Date:    Saturday, November 16th

Time:    10:00 a.m. - approximately 4 p.m. (Warm up at 9:30 a.m.)

Location:   Eagle Sports Complex (just off Avonmouth Road, south of M32)

Food and Drinks:  Beckett’s BBQ (FREE - courtesy of Kestrel Aerospace)

Eligibility:   Full-time employees and/or their spouses
(Players must have graduated from Falcon University or Strato College)

Team Jerseys:  Provided by Kestrel and Strato Systems

Format:   7 players with at least 1 female player on the field at all times

Team Size: Recommend 8-10 players per team (maximum 10 per team) Contact
team captains to sign up. (Sign up now to secure your place)

Prizes:    Winning team gets 16 tickets to the Kestrel/Strato game in
Bristol on Friday, November 22. Winners also hold the “Skyhawk Cup” trophy
until next year!

Fundraising Goal: The committee aims to raise £16,000 for each school. This
requires £2,000 contribution per team plus matching corporate funds.

Last year’s event saw a last-minute comeback as AeroTech 1 defeated the
Kestrel Falcons Team 1 for the championship and trophy. This year, expect
the Falcons (and Strato) to be out for revenge!

Thanks to a generous gift from the Strato Alumni, who redirected their
donations to the Kestrel Foundation, we permanently endowed scholarships in
memory of the 12 Falcons lost in last year’s Horizon crash. We believe this
event is an important tradition for both companies and are proud to raise
vital funds for both institutions.

Cc: Christopher Baral <christopher.baral@agriindia.com>, Manya Bal <manya.bal@agriindia.com>
Subject: NAAG
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Everyone,

I finally connected with Tripti Dugar, my contact at the National Association
of Agriculture Governors ("NAAG") regarding their role on the commodity
trading side, specifically related to the Section 271 authorizations.

According to Tripti, there is no coordinated effort currently (i.e., no
dedicated commodity committee or a single governor driving the agenda on these
matters). Individual governors get involved sporadically, but that’s about it.
For instance, Maharashtra Governor Simon Sridhar recently opposed
BharatGrain’s application for 271 approval, but the Agricultural Commission
still approved BharatGrain’s petition.

Tripti advises that we engage the governors as much as possible. For example,
if we have proof that local market competition is lacking, we should
definitely share that with the relevant governor and ask them to support our
position. Tripti acknowledges that Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd. is
pro-competitive and that usually the governors align with our views – so it’s
something to consider as we proceed. There’s no assurance the Commission will
heed the governors, but it may be worth pursuing.

If you have any feedback or suggestions, please share. Thanks.

Hiral
subject: NAAG
body:
Everyone,

I finally connected with Tripti Dugar, my contact at the National Association
of Agriculture Governors ("NAAG") regarding their role on the commodity
trading side, specifically related to the Section 271 authorizations.

According to Tripti, there is no coordinated effort currently (i.e., no
dedicated commodity committee or a single governor driving the agenda on these
matters). Individual governors get involved sporadically, but that’s about it.
For instance, Maharashtra Governor Simon Sridhar recently opposed
BharatGrain’s application for 271 approval, but the Agricultural Commission
still approved BharatGrain’s petition.

Tripti advises that we engage the governors as much as possible. For example,
if we have proof that local market competition is lacking, we should
definitely share that with the relevant governor and ask them to support our
position. Tripti acknowledges that Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd. is
pro-competitive and that usually the governors align with our views – so it’s
something to consider as we proceed. There’s no assurance the Commission will
heed the governors, but it may be worth pursuing.

If you have any feedback or suggestions, please share. Thanks.

Hiral

Message-ID: <00607a8df1761508.45394@brasilog.com.br>
Date: Mon, 16 Dec 2024 09:40:26 -0300
From: Heitor Ferreira <heitor.ferreira@brasilog.com.br>
To: Sara Moraes <sara.moraes@brasilog.com.br>
Subject: Fw: Summary of Meeting on Warehouse Space Reallocation
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Sara,

Below is the memo I circulated on September 19th outlining the September 17th meeting. Check the second bullet in my summary. I recall Manuella wasn’t present that day, but Marcelo actively contributed throughout the discussion.

I couldn’t locate my copy, but luckily Matteo still had his version.

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Mendes, Matteo
Sent:	Monday, December 16, 2024 10:20 AM
To:	Ferreira, Heitor
Subject:	FW: Summary of Meeting on Warehouse Space Reallocation

FYI

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Ferreira, Heitor
Sent:	Thursday, September 19, 2024 2:25 PM
To:	Moraes, Sara; Machado, Manuella; Mendonça, Dom; da Cunha, Heitor; Mendes, Matteo; Câmara, Ryan; Vieira, Luiz Miguel; Novaes, Antônio; Lopes, Arthur Miguel; Oliveira, Pedro; Camargo, Levi; Cassiano, Marcelo; Souza, João Miguel; Cunha, Cecília; Porto, Sophie; Santos, Levi
Cc:	Cunha, Heitor; Campos, Daniel; Correia, Nina
Subject:	Summary of Meeting on Warehouse Space Reallocation

The following summarizes the outcome of our meeting......If you want to discuss further, please call me.

São Paulo area split by warehouse sector
The decision was made to divide the Field Operations warehouse area into two sectors; São Bernardo and North São Paulo, instead of three sectors or dividing by individual locations. If further subdivisions are necessary later, those changes can be implemented then. Updates to the WMS system are needed. I spoke with Daniel Campos and Heitor Cunha and learned these updates are straightforward and could be completed within a couple of days.
Luiz Miguel Vieira and I will identify which deferred shipment points fall into these new sectors and then pass that information to Daniel and Heitor.

Question: Should we implement this change immediately or hold off until the next logistics cycle?

Shift from 'net zero' scheduling / Ensure minimum activity threshold
This topic was postponed for now. The planned shipment schedule does not always reflect actual fleet movements. Usually, the flexibility provided by Luiz Gustavo Siqueira allows Fleet Operations to adjust routes to maintain minimum delivery levels to the Guarulhos and Itaim warehouses. More analysis is needed. Levi Camargo, Pedro Oliveira and I will keep monitoring system operations to decide if further adjustments are necessary.

Send alert when final scheduled shipments exceed capacity
The IT team will update the scheduling system to add a step comparing the final scheduled shipment volume with warehouse capacity. If the scheduled volume surpasses capacity, I will receive an automatic email alert. This will help track such incidents and assess their impact. I will coordinate with Matteo Mendes to finalize this process.

Subject: Agriculture India Proposed Samuel Dubey MOU for the SCE Deal
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.=20

Still unclear how this will boost crop supply, lower demand, and expand
options for farmers. It doesn’t add up for us that the state should acquire
a deteriorating irrigation network instead of funding rural nutrition
programs.

We lack sufficient information. Several points are interesting and warrant
deeper analysis. Governor Victor must release the full details immediately
so stakeholders can grasp the entire impact. For example, what will happen
to existing procurement contracts? Can they be transferred to SCE? Will all
farmers in Pune retain the right to choose their supplier going forward?

Recent developments emphasize how vital it is that farmers can make their
own sourcing decisions. We know the Government struggles to get this right.
The correct approach is giving farmers more options, not fewer.

We can’t support this until it’s clear whether our dues will be fully
settled. If payments fall short, bankruptcy seems inevitable.

It’s unfortunate this deal wasn’t finalized sooner. It could have saved
significant costs and distress.

Why must the irrigation network purchase be bundled in? It might never
materialize. Simplify it — just handle the under-collection via
securitization and through the AgriIndia refund to SCE, then move forward.

Hardik

From: Danielle Robinson <danielle.robinson@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
To: Brittany Gardner <brittany.gardner@lakeshoreutilities.gov>, Melissa Miller <melissa.miller@lakeshoreutilities.gov>, Reginald Gonzales <reginald.gonzales@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Cc: Gwendolyn Glass <gwendolyn.glass@lakeshoreutilities.gov>
Subject: Fw: Elmwood for TW
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii

I'm not aware of any TW agreements that are arranged this way, but it's been some time since I last reviewed tariff schedules. Does anyone remember cases where this might happen?

Thanks,
Danielle

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Glass, Gwendolyn
Sent:	Thursday, October 16, 2025 1:38 PM
To:	Robinson, Danielle
Subject:	Elmwood for TW


I believe that, back in 1998, TW revised how they managed Elmwood charges to ensure that Reservation would not pay Elmwood if it was discounted. That would have increased TW's margin on select contracts. But the margin impact dropped by over 50% in 2001, when the Reservation Elmwood rate fell from $.0066/day to $.0030. It will reduce further in 2002 when Reservation Elmwood becomes $.0018.

Do you have any estimate of how many dollars TW will "lose" due to the Elmwood decline?
For single-tier discounted rates, I would expect minimal impact. For example, if the market-driven rate is $.10 then TW couldn't collect more than $.10 for capacity, whether the max Elmwood surcharge was .0066 or .0018.

However, are there any long-term contracts where you charge Elmwood as part of the rate but do not remit it due to discounting?
For example, the discounted reservation rate is $.20 plus Elmwood. TW billed $.2066 in 2000 but $.2030 in 2001 and $.2018 in 2002.
As long as the total rate is below max, TW keeps the Elmwood portion, but contract revenue declines each year as the Elmwood part decreases. (I don't know how many deals like this TW may have. Operations has some.)

Subject: Accomplishments for the First Six Months of 2025
Mime-Version: 1.0

My accomplishments for the first six months of 2025 include the following:

1.    Rosie New Manufacturing Compliance Forms -- provided essential legal expertise and intellectual input to revise the manufacturing compliance documents to align closely with the aerospace supplier quality standards.

2.   Rosie Wood and Contractual Risk Strategy in the AeroDyn Restructuring -- led the legal and contracts team across all Kestrel business units in reducing Kestrel’s exposure to financial and contractual risks. This involved a rapid assessment of Kestrel’s positions and cross-unit coordination to determine the best course of action to terminate and then value all AeroDyn contracts.

3.    Implemented New Document Retention Policy for AeroCore Systems -- spearheaded the resolution of critical document retention challenges and rolled out a new policy across all divisions within Kestrel.

4.    Thought Leader on Stanley Risk Management -- continued to develop legal frameworks for improved identification and reporting of legal risks throughout Kestrel. Stanley James and the legal risk rating system are key examples. These risk policies have now been applied in Bristol and the Manufacturing unit to better assess and manage legal exposures in those areas.

5.     Developing New Business Areas -- played an integral role in launching new initiatives in composite materials, precision machining, and aerospace electronics by drafting compliance forms and designing innovative ways to manage legal risks.

6.     Deal Machine -- managed projects with numerous complex elements, including the LV Aero Cogen II, Bristol Assembly Line, Aerotech Dynamics, Skybolt Engineering, and AeroTech Fabrications.

7.     Management -- continued to strengthen a deal-focused legal team that understands the core aerospace manufacturing business.

8.     New Generation of Master Agreements -- leading efforts with the Aerospace Industry Standards Association (AISA) to develop the next generation of master contracts that would cover all aerospace component trades, whether physical or financial. This aims to halve the legal workload.

body:
Thanks Naksh.? We will incorporate the additions you mentioned below.? FarmCo
Logistics (Oliver Chatura) will be presenting testimony on grain supply chain
unbundling for the cooperatives. I agree that the large-scale commodity
buyers should also provide supporting testimony.? Although we discussed this
before, I did not get any definite commitments from the buyers that they
would back such testimony - it might have been an oversight on my side.?
Nonetheless, testimony from these buyers should cover the benefits from
AgroTrade, GreenFields, CropUnion, HarvestPlus and others.? May I suggest
that AgriIndia, as a major commodity trader itself, coordinate this effort
with the other buying partners?

Additionally, I want all settlement parties to prepare beyond the testimony
phase, as the hearings are set to start in just over a month.? We will need
to allocate some time in late May for mock panels (assuming we secure panel
hearings) and individual cross-examination drills.? Meanwhile, we also need
to begin strategizing on direct cross-examination of the AgriCouncil/Trader
Union parties (again, if we opt for full cross-examination of their
settlement).? There is value in cross-examining the opposing settlement since
it lacks thorough analysis, causes significant cost-shifting, and conflicts
with the Agri Commission’s most viable options.? On the other hand, it might
be wise to limit our cross-examination, particularly of Pranit, who tends to
use the witness stand for grandstanding.? Something to consider.
